mainTopic: Which coin the word כסף means: in the תורה versus in the words of the חכמים
overview: רב אסי teaches that when the תורה says כסף, it means the valuable Tyrian coin (כסף צורי), while amounts set by the חכמים use the cheaper local coin (כסף מדינה). The גמרא tests this with four cases where the תורה says כסף but a small or copper coin is allowed. For a court claim (טענה), the amount comes from pairing כסף with כלים. For מעשר שני, the repeated word כסף widens the rule, and הקדש learns the same from מעשר שני through the word קודש. But קידושין has no such exception, and רב אסי cannot be holding like בית שמאי. So the גמרא restates his rule: only a fixed sum (כסף קצוב) in the תורה is in Tyrian silver. Since the משנה already teaches that, his real new point is that rabbinic sums are in local coin. For example, the 'סלע' fine for striking someone is only half a זוז. A story about רב הונא and חנן the wicked shows this fine in practice, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: תורה money means Tyrian coins; rabbinic money means local coins
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב אסי: plain כסף in the תורה is כסף צורי, and כסף in the words of the חכמים is כסף מדינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: Every time the תורה says 'money' without saying which coin, it means Tyrian coins. When the חכמים mention money, it means local coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a general rule about which coin is meant when the word כסף appears. The תורה uses the valuable coin and the חכמים use the cheaper one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כסף צורי was the high-value standard silver coin, and כסף מדינה was worth about one-eighth of it. The rule only covers a plain mention of money (סתם). In those cases, an amount in the תורה is much bigger than the same number in the words of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Tyrian silver coinage, the full-value coin
Provincial (local) coinage, worth about one-eighth of the Tyrian coin
Without details; stated plainly
Their words, meaning the words of the חכמים (rabbinic statements)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides the real value of every amount of money mentioned in the תורה, such as fines and redemption payments.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
Every 'money' stated in the Torah without detail —
is Tyrian coinage,
phrases.notes: The high-value coin

phrases.english: and that of their (the Sages') words — is provincial coinage.
phrases.notes: Worth about one-eighth of the Tyrian coin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic on the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain כסף in the תורה means כסף צורי. כסף in the words of the חכמים means כסף מדינה.

steps.title: Challenge from the minimum amount of a court claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this is really a fixed rule. In the verse about a deposit, the תורה says כסף, yet the משנה sets the minimum claim for a שבועה at only two silver מעה, not Tyrian coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really a rule? But look at the case of a claim, where it is written: 'If a man gives his friend money or vessels to guard.' And we learned in a משנה: the oath of the judges requires a claim of at least two silver coins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אסי's rule with a case where the תורה says plain כסף but the הלכה does not use the Tyrian coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about deposits says כסף, and from that section we learn the שבועת הדיינין. If רב אסי were right, the minimum claim should be measured in Tyrian coins. Instead the משנה requires only 'שתי כסף', two silver מעה, which is a small amount. So it looks like plain כסף in the תורה does not always mean Tyrian coinage.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it a fixed rule? (an opening for a challenge)
A monetary claim brought to court
The oath given by the judges to a defendant who admits to part of the claim
Two silver מעה, the minimum claim needed
And we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'שתי כסף' here does not mean two Tyrian coins. It means two small silver מעה. That gap is exactly why it is a challenge.

phrases.english: And is it a fixed rule?
But there is the case of a claim, as it is written:
'If a man gives to his neighbor
money or vessels to guard,'
phrases.notes: שמות כב:ו

phrases.english: and we learned in a mishna: The oath of the judges —
phrases.notes: שבועות לח:

phrases.english: requires that the claim be two silver (ma'ah)!
phrases.notes: A small amount, not Tyrian coinage

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule of step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that plain כסף in the תורה means כסף צורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse says plain כסף, yet the הלכה's minimum is two small silver מעה rather than Tyrian coinage, so this seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: A claim is different because money is paired with vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case of טענה is different. The verse says 'כסף או כלים', so each word teaches about the other: כסף must be at least two, like כלים, and כלים must be valuable, like כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written 'money or vessels'. Just as 'vessels' means at least two, so 'money' means at least two. And just as money is something valuable, so the vessels must be something valuable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. It says the claim case does not follow the plain rule, because there the amount is learned from the comparison between כסף and כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's rule is only for plain, unpaired כסף. In the deposit verse, כסף sits next to כלים, and the plural כלים teaches that the claim must be at least 'two'. So the minimum of two silver מעה comes from this comparison, not from the normal meaning of כסף. The comparison also works the other way: the vessels must have real value, like money.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; a standard way of answering by setting a case apart
Just as ... so too; the form of a comparison between two words
A significant, valuable item
Vessels, objects (plural, meaning at least two)

steps.whatToRemember: The minimum claim of two מעה does not contradict רב אסי, because that amount comes from pairing כסף with כלים, not from plain כסף. (רב אסי's rule itself is narrowed later, in step 9.)
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא protects a general rule: it limits the rule to plain mentions and explains the exception through a special source in the verse.

phrases.english: It is different there, as it is written:
'money or vessels,'
phrases.notes: The two words are paired, so each teaches about the other

phrases.aramaic: מָה כֵּלִים שְׁנַיִם — אַף כֶּסֶף שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: just as 'vessels' means two — so too 'money' means two,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כֶּסֶף דָּבָר חָשׁוּב — אַף כֵּלִים דָּבָר חָשׁוּב.
phrases.english: and just as money is a significant item — so too vessels must be a significant item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by setting the claim case apart
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני התם): the source is a comparison between two words, not plain כסף
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The minimum of two silver מעה for a claim seemed to show that plain כסף in the תורה is not Tyrian coinage.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim amount comes from comparing כסף with כלים, so רב אסי's rule for plain כסף still stands.

steps.title: Challenge from second tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says כסף about redeeming מעשר שני, yet a משנה shows copper coins can be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about מעשר שני? It is written: 'And bind up the money (כסף) in your hand.' And yet we learned in a משנה about someone who exchanges a סלע for copper coins of מעשר שני. So copper coins work, not only Tyrian silver.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case to attack רב אסי's rule. The תורה uses the word כסף for מעשר שני, but the משנה lets a person use copper coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If plain כסף in the תורה always meant Tyrian silver, then מעשר שני could only be redeemed with silver coins. But the משנה about exchanging a סלע for copper מעות shows that copper coins also count as מעשר שני money. So the rule seems to fail here.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that is eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
And you shall bind up (the money)
One who breaks a larger coin into smaller change
Small coins, here copper coins

phrases.english: But there is the case of tithe,
as it is written: 'And bind up the money in your hand,'
phrases.notes: דברים יד:כה, about redeeming second tithe

phrases.english: and we learned: one who exchanges a sela
phrases.notes: משנה מעשר שני ב:ח

phrases.english: for copper coins of second tithe!
phrases.notes: This shows copper coins can serve as מעשר שני money

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the טענה case was explained, the גמרא brings a new counterexample to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that כסף in the תורה means כסף צורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה says כסף for מעשר שני, yet copper coins are allowed. So כסף cannot always mean Tyrian silver.

steps.title: The repeated word money widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: The תורה repeats the word כסף about מעשר שני, and that repetition includes any kind of coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה says 'money' and 'money' again. This repetition comes to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מעשר שני is a special case. The תורה repeats the word כסף there, and that extra wording comes to include all kinds of coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's rule still holds in general. In מעשר שני the תורה says כסף more than once, and the extra word is a רִיבּוּי, an inclusion that widens the meaning. So here the תורה itself tells us that copper coins are also fine.

keyTerms.meaning: It included more; an extra word that widens the law

phrases.english: 'Money,' 'money': it included more.
phrases.notes: The word כסף appears more than once in the מעשר שני passage (דברים יד:כה–כו)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מעשר שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse: a repeated word creates an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Copper coins working for מעשר שני proves כסף never means Tyrian silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general rule stands. מעשר שני is an exception because the repeated word widens it to all coins.

steps.title: Challenge from redeeming consecrated property
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says כסף about redeeming הקדש, yet שמואל says something worth a פרוטה redeems it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about הקדש? It is written: 'And he will give the money (כסף) and it will be his.' And שמואל said: הקדש worth a מנה that was redeemed for something worth a פרוטה is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case. For הקדש the תורה also says כסף, yet שמואל says even something worth one tiny פרוטה can redeem it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כסף meant Tyrian silver, you would need a silver coin to redeem הקדש. But שמואל says that even an item worth one copper פרוטה works (after the fact), even when the הקדש is worth a hundred דינר. So again the תורה's כסף does not seem to require Tyrian silver.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
A large sum, one hundred דינר
The smallest copper coin
Redeemed; the holiness has been moved off it

phrases.english: But there is the case of consecrated property,
as it is written: 'And he will give the money and it will be his,'
phrases.notes: Based on ויקרא כז:יט

phrases.english: and שמואל said: consecrated property worth a maneh
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred דינר

phrases.english: that one redeemed onto something worth a peruta is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering מעשר שני, the גמרא brings a new counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that כסף in the תורה means כסף צורי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה says כסף for הקדש, yet a פרוטה's worth redeems it. So כסף is not limited to Tyrian silver.

steps.title: Consecrated property learns from second tithe
steps.stepSummary: הקדש learns from מעשר שני through the shared word קדש, so it shares that same exception.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הקדש is also a special case. It is linked to מעשר שני by the shared word קודש, so it gets the same wide rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קודש appears in the הקדש passage and also in the מעשר passage. This creates a גזירה שוה, a word-link that compares the two laws. Since מעשר שני already allows any coin, הקדש does too. רב אסי's general rule is untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: Learns, derives
The shared word 'holy' that links two passages (a גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה)

phrases.english: Consecrated property also derives
'holy,' 'holy' from tithe.
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:יד and כז:ל both use the word קודש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הקדש challenge by linking it to the answer given for מעשר שני.
steps.terutzResolutionType: גזירה שוה: borrowing an exception from another case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Redeeming הקדש with a פרוטה proves כסף does not mean Tyrian silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש shares the מעשר שני exception through the word קודש, so the general rule stands.

steps.title: Challenge from betrothing a woman
steps.stepSummary: קידושין is done with כסף from the Torah, yet בית הלל allow a פרוטה. Would רב אסי really follow בית שמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about betrothing a woman? It is written: 'She shall go out for nothing, without money (כסף).' And we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say a woman is betrothed with a דינר or something worth a דינר, and בית הלל say with a פרוטה or something worth a פרוטה. Shall we say that רב אסי follows בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth case, קידושי אשה. This time it finds no special verse to save the rule. It asks whether רב אסי holds like בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'אין כסף' teaches that a woman is acquired with כסף. If כסף meant a silver coin, you would need at least a דינר, which is בית שמאי's view. But the הלכה follows בית הלל, who allow a copper פרוטה. It would be very strange for רב אסי to follow the rejected view of בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A silver coin, much more valuable than a פרוטה
Shall we say? (often raising an unwanted conclusion)
The two great schools; הלכה usually follows בית הלל

steps.confusionAlert: The verse 'ויצאה חנם אין כסף' is about a maidservant going free without paying. The גמרא uses it as the source that a woman can be acquired (betrothed) with כסף. Do not get stuck on its simple context.

phrases.english: But there is the betrothal of a woman,
as it is written: 'She shall go out for nothing, without money,'
phrases.notes: שמות כא:יא

phrases.english: and we learned: בית שמאי say:
phrases.notes: משנה קידושין א:א

phrases.english: with a dinar or with something worth a dinar,
and בית הלל say:
with a peruta or with something worth a peruta,

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא רַב אַסִּי דְּאָמַר כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי?
phrases.english: shall we say that Rav Asi spoke in line with בית שמאי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After three cases were answered (טענה, מעשר שני, הקדש), a fourth case is raised that has no special exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's rule that all plain כסף in the תורה means Tyrian silver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule were true, קידושין would need a silver coin, which is בית שמאי's view. That puts רב אסי against the accepted הלכה of בית הלל.

steps.title: רב אסי's rule restated for fixed amounts only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב אסי: only a set, fixed sum in the Torah is in Tyrian silver, and rabbinic sums are in local coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב יהודה said in the name of רב אסי: every fixed sum of money mentioned in the תורה is Tyrian silver, and fixed sums of the חכמים are local coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the broad version of רב אסי's rule and says he actually taught a narrower rule. Only a fixed amount of money in the תורה is measured in Tyrian silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original version said every plain כסף means Tyrian silver, and the קידושין case broke it. The new version applies only when the תורה sets a specific sum, such as fifty שקלים. Plain mentions of 'money' like קידושין, מעשר שני and הקדש are not covered, so a פרוטה can work there and בית הלל fits.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said; the גמרא corrects the wording of a teaching
Fixed, set (a specific amount)
Of their words; amounts set by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רב אסי: a FIXED sum in the תורה (like fifty שקלים) is paid in כסף צורי. A rabbinic fixed sum is paid in כסף מדינה. A plain mention of 'money' with no set amount, like קידושין, does not need Tyrian silver.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why many תורה payments, such as fines and redemptions with a set amount, are calculated in the heavier Tyrian silver. Rabbinic amounts, like a כתובה, use the lighter local coin.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav Asi said:
every fixed sum of money stated in the Torah
is Tyrian silver,
and that of their (rabbinic) words is local coinage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The קידושין challenge cannot be answered, so the גמרא changes the wording of the original statement from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אסי's rule applies only to fixed sums: fixed תורה amounts are in כסף צורי and fixed rabbinic amounts are in כסף מדינה. Plain unspecified כסף, as in קידושין, can be a פרוטה, which matches בית הלל.

steps.title: What does רב אסי add if the משנה already says this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אסי's statement as unnecessary, because the משנה already says the Torah's fixed sums are in Tyrian silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב אסי teaching us? We already learned in the משנה that the five סלעים for a firstborn son, and the other תורה sums, are paid in the שקל הקודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רב אסי needed to say his rule at all, since our משנה already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 restated רב אסי: fixed תורה sums are paid in Tyrian silver. But the משנה already lists these sums, such as the five סלעים of פדיון הבן, and says they are paid in the שקל הקודש. So the first half of his statement seems to repeat the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)
We already learned it (in a משנה or ברייתא)
The five סלעים paid to redeem a firstborn son (פדיון הבן)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: Aimed at רב אסי's rule from step 9.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנֵינָא: חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים שֶׁל בֵּן וְכוּ׳!
phrases.english: We already learned: 'The five סלעים of a son, etc.'!
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה's list (slave, rapist, seducer, slanderer).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the restated rule of רב אסי from step 9 adds anything to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's statement that תורה fixed sums are in Tyrian silver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule already stated explicitly in the משנה does not need to be taught again by an אמורא.

steps.title: His real point is that rabbinic sums use local coin
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי was needed to teach that sums set by the חכמים are in local coin. For example, the 'סלע' fine for striking someone is only half a זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needed to teach the part about rabbinic sums being in local coin. As we learned: one who strikes his fellow gives him a סלע. Do not say this is a סלע worth four זוזים. Rather, it is half a זוז, because people call half a זוז a 'סלע'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new point is the second half of רב אסי's rule: amounts set by the חכמים are paid in local, cheaper coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only covers תורה sums. רב אסי adds that when the חכמים set an amount, such as the סלע fine for striking someone, the 'סלע' is the local coin people call by that name, which is worth just half a זוז. Without his rule, we might think the striker owes a full Tyrian סלע of four זוזים, eight times as much.

keyTerms.meaning: Sums set by the words of the חכמים (rabbinic), not by the Torah
Local or provincial coin, worth less than Tyrian silver
It was necessary for him (to teach this)
One who strikes his fellow, as an insult
Half a זוז (half a dinar)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word 'סלע' means two very different amounts. In a תורה sum it is a Tyrian סלע of four זוזים. In a rabbinic fine it is the local 'סלע', worth only half a זוז.
steps.whatToRemember: תורה fixed sums are paid in Tyrian silver. Sums set by the חכמים are paid in local coin, so the 'סלע' fine for striking someone is half a זוז.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the actual amount owed for the rabbinic fine for striking someone, as the next story shows.

phrases.english: And that sums of their (the Sages') words are local coin
phrases.notes: This is the new half of רב אסי's rule.

phrases.english: was necessary for him to teach,
as we learned: One who strikes his fellow
phrases.notes: משנה in בבא קמא 90a.

phrases.english: gives him a סלע,
and do not say a סלע of four זוזים,
phrases.notes: That is the Tyrian סלע.

phrases.english: rather, half a זוז,
since people call half a זוז a 'סלע'.
phrases.notes: The name follows common local usage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל דִּבְרֵיהֶם כֶּסֶף מְדִינָה אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by moving the focus of רב אסי's rule to its second clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the necessary chiddush: the rule's second clause is not found in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי's statement merely repeats the משנה's list of תורה sums in Tyrian silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: His point is that rabbinic sums, like the striking fine, are paid in local coin: half a זוז, not four זוזים.

steps.title: רב הונא orders a striker to pay half a זוז
steps.stepSummary: חנן the wicked struck a man, and רב הונא ruled that he must pay half a זוז, applying רב אסי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנן the wicked struck a certain man. The case came before רב הונא, who told him: Give him half a זוז. He had (the story continues)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the rule in practice. רב הונא sets the striking fine at half a זוז. The story continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real case of the rabbinic 'סלע' fine. רב הונא applies the local-coin value from step 11, half a זוז, not four זוזים. The last words 'הוה איכא' begin the next part of the story, where חנן uses the cheap fine to his advantage.
